Q: IndexError: list index out of range in Python - how to capture the last item in a list? A:

you can try using my_list[-1]
it is called list slicing where -1 means last element of the array and -2 means second last.

Q: Immvision thinks ndarray not being passed while type() shows it is A:

I don't know why but code works when I create new array

img_array = np.zeros((self.height, self.width, 4), dtype=np.uint8)

It seems it has the same size, shape, dtype but for some reason it works.

I found that code also work when I convert your array to np.array()

img_array = np.frombuffer(buf, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(h, w, 4)

img_array = np.array(img_array)

I may only guess that original img_array keeps data as view to different places in memory but C/C++ code may need object in contiguous memory.

Differences shows img_array.flags.

By the way:

There are other problems in code.

It needs get_window_pos() instead of get_window_position(). (small typo)

Other problem is that immvision.GlTexture(img_array) gives object GlTexture, not number texture ID and variable self.texture_id can be missleading because in some places it needs self.texture_id.texture_id to get real texture ID.

In one place it also needs to get texture ref instead of texture id

imgui.image(
    imgui.ImTextureRef(self.texture_id.texture_id),
    ImVec2(self.width, self.height),
)

After changes I get this:

Full working code:

import io
import os

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import cartopy
import cartopy.crs as ccrs
import cartopy.feature as cfeature
from imgui_bundle import imgui, immvision, ImVec2, immapp


def info(arr):
    print("--- arr ---")
    print(f"size: {arr.size}")
    print(f"shape: {arr.shape}")
    print(f"type: {type(arr)}")
    print(f"dtype: {arr.dtype}")
    print(f"strides: {arr.strides}")
    print(f"flags:\n{arr.flags}", end="")
    print(f"base: {arr.base}")
    print("---")


class MapApp:
    def __init__(self):
        # Base map bounding box
        self.base_lat_min, self.base_lat_max = 3, 5
        self.base_lon_min, self.base_lon_max = -10, -7

        # Current zoom extents start as base extents
        self.lat_min, self.lat_max = self.base_lat_min, self.base_lat_max
        self.lon_min, self.lon_max = self.base_lon_min, self.base_lon_max

        self.fig, self.ax = plt.subplots(
            figsize=(8, 6), subplot_kw={"projection": ccrs.PlateCarree()}
        )
        self.texture = None
        self.needs_redraw = True

        self.width, self.height = 800, 600  # Image display size

        self.zoom_factor = 1.0  # 1.0 means no zoom
        cartopy.config["pre_existing_data_dir"] = os.getcwd()
        cartopy.config["data_dir"] = os.getcwd()

    def update_map_texture(self):
        self.ax.clear()
        self.ax.set_extent(
            [self.lon_min, self.lon_max, self.lat_min, self.lat_max],
            crs=ccrs.PlateCarree(),
        )
        self.ax.coastlines("50m")
        self.ax.add_feature(cfeature.BORDERS, linestyle=":")
        self.ax.add_feature(cfeature.LAND, facecolor="lightgray")
        self.ax.add_feature(cfeature.OCEAN, facecolor="lightblue")

        canvas = self.fig.canvas
        canvas.draw()
        w, h = canvas.get_width_height()
        print(f"w: {w}, h: {h}")

        buf = canvas.tostring_argb()
        img_array = np.frombuffer(buf, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(h, w, 4)
        # img_array = np.zeros((self.height, self.width, 4), dtype=np.uint8)
        info(img_array)

        img_array = np.array(img_array)
        info(img_array)

        if self.texture is None:
            self.texture = immvision.GlTexture(img_array)
            print(
                f"texture: {self.texture} | texture.texture_id: {self.texture.texture_id}"
            )
        else:
            immvision.GlTexture.update_from_image(self.texture, img_array, False)

        self.needs_redraw = False

    def gui(self):
        imgui.begin("Interactive Map with Zoom")

        if self.needs_redraw or self.texture is None:
            self.update_map_texture()

        imgui.image(
            imgui.ImTextureRef(
                self.texture.texture_id
            ),  # needs `.texture_id` and `ImTextureRef()`
            ImVec2(self.width, self.height),
        )

        # Mouse position and coordinate display
        mouse_pos = imgui.get_mouse_pos()
        window_pos = imgui.get_window_pos()  # ERROR: position
        cursor_pos = imgui.get_cursor_pos()
        image_pos = (window_pos.x + cursor_pos.x, window_pos.y + cursor_pos.y)

        rel_x = mouse_pos.x - image_pos[0]
        rel_y = mouse_pos.y - image_pos[1]

        if 0 <= rel_x < self.width and 0 <= rel_y < self.height:
            lon = self.lon_min + (rel_x / self.width) * (self.lon_max - self.lon_min)
            lat = self.lat_max - (rel_y / self.height) * (self.lat_max - self.lat_min)
            imgui.text(f"Mouse Lon: {lon:.4f}  Lat: {lat:.4f}")

        imgui.end()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = MapApp()
    immapp.run(gui_function=app.gui, window_title="imgui Cartopy Map with Zoom")

Idea for np.zeros() I found in demo demos_python/demos_imgui_explorer/implot3d_demo.py which I found on GitHub repo imgui_bundle. There are more demos.

Q: Telegram Mini App (WebView) loads forever on Android A:

What you’re seeing is most likely a compatibility issue between Telegram Android’s embedded WebView and Cloudflare’s proxied TLS/edge setup, not a problem with Next.js or Railway itself.

The biggest clue is this:

  • it works on iOS, macOS, desktop browsers, and Chrome on Android

  • it works when you use the Railway direct domain

  • it works when you disable Cloudflare proxy

  • it also works when you keep Cloudflare proxy on but disable TLS 1.3

That strongly suggests the failure is happening before the actual HTTP request reaches your app, during the connection handshake phase. That matches your observation that the page is not even requested when opened from Telegram on Android.

So the issue is probably not your application code. It is more likely one of these:

  • a TLS 1.3 negotiation issue

  • a QUIC / HTTP/3 issue

  • an incompatibility in how Telegram Android’s WebView handles Cloudflare’s edge connection

  • less likely, but still possible: a stricter certificate/chain expectation in Telegram Android

Since disabling TLS 1.3 fixes it, that is the strongest signal. In practice, Telegram Android’s in-app browser appears to be more fragile than normal Chrome in some network setups, especially behind proxies/CDNs.

A few important notes:

  1. This is probably not Railway
    Railway works directly, so your origin is fine.

  2. This is probably not a basic certificate problem
    If Cloudflare is terminating TLS, Cloudflare handles the public certificate chain. So unless there is something very unusual in your SSL setup, the more likely culprit is the edge protocol negotiation, not the origin cert.

  3. Cloudflare proxy is the trigger
    Since DNS-only mode works, the issue is clearly introduced by Cloudflare’s proxy layer.

If you want to keep Cloudflare enabled, the safest practical setup is:

  • keep SSL mode = Full (strict)

  • disable TLS 1.3 for that hostname if necessary

  • also test disabling HTTP/3 / QUIC

  • make sure there are no WAF challenges, Bot Fight Mode, or managed challenges on the Mini App route

  • avoid any Cloudflare features that modify responses aggressively on that subdomain

If you want a cleaner production setup, I would recommend putting the Telegram Mini App on a dedicated subdomain with a simpler Cloudflare policy, for example:

  • proxy on

  • Full (strict)

  • TLS 1.2 allowed

  • TLS 1.3 off if needed

  • HTTP/3 off

  • no challenge pages

  • minimal caching/security transformations

So in short: yes, this looks like a Cloudflare edge compatibility issue with Telegram Android, and the fact that disabling TLS 1.3 fixes it is a very strong indicator that the problem is in TLS/protocol negotiation, not in your app.
